claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a Christian priest (presbyter) and exegete active during the first half of the fifth century.
Hesychius served as a presbyter in the church in Jerusalem around 412.
Hesychius was renowned in the Eastern Church as a theologian, biblical commentator, and preacher who was acclaimed as having annotated the whole of sacred Scripture.
The Homilia de jejunio (On Fasting) is homily number 15 in the collection of Hesychius's sermons.
The Homilia de jejunio was written for the first week of the holy Forty Days of the fast (Lent).
The Homilia de jejunio survives in manuscript Sinai gr. 491 from Saint Catherine's Monastery at Mount Sinai.
The Pappas Patristic Institute's translation of On Fasting was, to their knowledge, the first time this text had appeared in English.
Hesychius's sermons include the earliest extant homily on the Meeting of the Lord, a feast that originated in Jerusalem.
Hesychius opposed Nestorius and lived during the period of the Third Ecumenical Council (Ephesus 431).
